hero.title: About this template
hero.description: A small, readable baseline for multilingual content sites built on TanStack Start.

sections.title: Why it exists
sections.body: Most starters either skip internationalization or bolt it on after the routing and SEO work is done. This template puts locale handling, metadata, and content authoring in place first, so the parts that are painful to retrofit are already correct.

sections.title: How routing works
sections.body: A single optional locale segment wraps the route tree. The default locale stays unprefixed, so the canonical URL is /blog rather than /en/blog. Visiting a prefixed default-locale URL returns a 301 to the clean form.

sections.title: How content works
sections.body: Interface copy lives in typed JSON namespaces under src/messages, merged over the English fallback and lazy-loaded per locale. Blog posts live in content/blogs as MDX, validated with Zod and compiled into static HTML at build time.

sections.title: What is intentionally left out
sections.body: There is no authentication, database, API layer, or analytics. Those choices depend on your product, and a template that guesses wrong costs more to remove than to add.

highlights.title: Included in the box
items: Localized routing with an unprefixed default locale
Per-page canonical, hreflang, Open Graph, and JSON-LD
Generated sitemap with alternate language links
MDX blog collection with locale-aware slugs
Light and dark themes with no flash on first paint
